অভ্যন্তরীণ সম্পদ বিভাগ
(কাস্টমস)

প্রজ্ঞাপন

তারিখ: ১৫ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪৩১ বঙ্গাব্দ/ ২৯ মে, ২০২৪ খ্রিষ্টাব্দ

এস.আর.ও. নং ২৩১-আইন/২০২৪/৫৩/কাস্টমস।— সরকার, কাস্টমস আইন, ২০২৩ (২০২৩ সনের ৫৭ নং আইন) এর ধারা ২৬৩, ধারা ১১ ও ১২ এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, ওয়্যারহাউস লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০২৪ এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

উপরিউক্ত বিধিমালার-

Customs Act 2023: The Government is empowered under Section 263, read with Sections 11 and 12, to issue regulations and amendments regarding customs procedures.
This Act provides the foundational authority for the government to act in consultation with the National Board of Revenue to amend warehouse licensing rules.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with the National Board of Revenue before exercising its legal authority to amend the warehouse licensing rules.
Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024: These rules are subject to further amendment by the government under the powers granted by the Customs Act 2023.

Deemed Exporter: This is defined as an industrial unit that produces and supplies accessories to a 100% export-oriented industry against a Back-to-Back Letter of Credit.

It also includes industrial units holding warehouse licenses in Export Processing Zones or Economic Zones that supply goods or services to other warehouse-licensed entities against domestic letters of credit denominated in foreign currency.
Back-to-Back Letter of Credit: This financial mechanism is used as the basis for defining industrial units that supply inputs for export-oriented production.
Joint Deemed and Direct Exporter: This is defined as an industrial entity that exports a portion of its produced goods directly abroad and supplies the remaining portion to direct exporters as backward linkage against a Back-to-Back Letter of Credit.

The definition also encompasses warehouse-licensed units in Export Processing Zones or Economic Zones that engage in both direct exports and the supply of goods or services to other warehouse-licensed entities against foreign currency-denominated domestic letters of credit.

Bangladesh Economic Zones Act 2010: The Act is cited as the governing legal framework for defining various processing areas, industrial units, and commercial zones eligible for specific customs or bonded privileges.
Domestic Consumption Bonded Warehouse: This entity is recognized as a license holder capable of receiving goods or services for processing from bonded industrial units within economic zones or export processing zones.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: The amendment clarifies the eligibility criteria for industrial units and service providers, including those operating under bonded facilities, to supply processed goods or services to export-oriented units or domestic tariff areas in foreign currency.

Warehouse License: The regulations require license holders to notify the licensing authority of any significant changes in the management or ownership structure of their business.
An application for updating these changes must be submitted on the official letterhead of the business within a specific timeframe following approval by the relevant regulatory bodies.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for receiving official applications regarding changes in business ownership or management for entities operating under a warehouse license.
Schedule-3: This schedule specifies the required documentation that must be submitted to the licensing authority when notifying changes in the management or ownership of a licensed warehouse business.

Statutory Regulatory Order: The legal instrument comes into effect immediately upon issuance.
